findings.evidence: Basic.lean:427 `private theorem ofConv_mul_apply (w) (x) : (LinearMap.mul' k (ConvolutionDual k H) w).ofConv x = dualDistribEquiv k H w (Coalgebra.comul x)`; at `w = phi ⊗ₜ psi` this is exactly Functoriality.lean:234-237 by `LinearMap.mul'_apply`.
findings.fix: Move `ofConv_mul_apply` out of the `HopfAlgebra` section (it uses only `mul'_apply`, `convMul_apply`, `comul` on `H` and `dualDistribEquiv_tmul_apply`, so `[Bialgebra k H]` from the section at Basic.lean:293 suffices), drop `private`, and derive the pure-tensor form as `LinearMap.mul'_apply ▸ ofConv_mul_apply k H (phi ⊗ₜ psi) x`; delete `convMul_apply_eq_dualDistribEquiv`'s proof and use the shared lemma in the `map_mul'` calc as well.
findings.issue: `convMul_apply_eq_dualDistribEquiv` re-proves the existing private `ofConv_mul_apply` (TauCeti/Algebra/HopfAlgebra/FiniteDual/Basic.lean:427), whose `tmul` case is the verbatim same `rw [LinearMap.convMul_apply]; generalize Coalgebra.comul … = z; induction z` script (Basic.lean:436-445 vs Functoriality.lean:238-245). The same computation appears a third time inline in the `evalAlgHom.map_mul'` calc block (Functoriality.lean:217-224).

findings.evidence: Basic.lean:447-466 and 468-487 differ only in which slot carries the antipode; Functoriality.lean:92-101 is the same statement with `mapAlgHom k f` in both slots, whose underlying map is `mapLinear k f = (WithConv.linearEquiv).symm ∘ₗ f.toLinearMap.dualMap ∘ₗ (WithConv.linearEquiv)` (Functoriality.lean:56-59).
findings.fix: State once in Basic.lean, for `f g : H →ₗ[k] K`: `dualDistribEquiv k H (TensorProduct.map ((WithConv.linearEquiv k _).symm ∘ₗ f.dualMap ∘ₗ (WithConv.linearEquiv k _)) (… g …) w) z = dualDistribEquiv k K w (TensorProduct.map f g z)`, and derive the two antipode lemmas (`K = H`, `g = id` / `f = id`, defeq to the antipode instance) and the new `mapAlgHom` case (`f = g = f.toLinearMap`) from it.
findings.issue: `dualDistribEquiv_tensor_map_apply` re-derives transpose-compatibility of `dualDistribEquiv`, already proved twice in Basic.lean:447 (`dualDistribEquiv_map_antipode_left_apply`) and Basic.lean:468 (`_right_apply`) with the identical double `TensorProduct.induction_on` script; the dual antipode is by definition the wrapped `dualMap` (Basic.lean:416-420), so all three are instances of one statement.

summary: The functor and double-dual equivalence are new material and reuse Mathlib well, but two of the new private lemmas re-derive computations already proved in FiniteDual/Basic.lean; the existing lemmas need to be generalized/exposed and reused instead.
